notes.title: Development Update | Bandit's Hollow
notes.content:
Hi all, it's crazy to think that Tundralia has been out for nearly 6 months now and what a time it's been. We've seen a lot bugs fixed and quality of life improvements made, as well as the addition of Hunters Rise and The Hollow Vault, but what's next I hear you cry?

Well without spoiling too much, patch 0.3.0 will extend the main storyline and add an additional 2 levels, bringing the max level to 12. This is alongside new level 12 class abilities, new side quests to complete and a new dungeon to explore.

As you can imagine, we're working hard on getting this patch ready and all going well, we are aiming to have this live by mid July. But in the meantime, here's a sneak peak at where we are heading next in the main story.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/a0f0be37b3b850a156a354287e7cfb497ad42991.png[/img]
Thanks again to everyone who has been playing the game and leaving feedback on the Steam discussion board. Tundralia is my passion project that I code outside of my 9 till 5 job so it's been amazing to see you all playing and enjoying the game, as well as hearing your suggestions for how to make it even better, so keep it coming!

notes.title: Development Update | Hunter's Rise Part 2
notes.content:
Hi all, to keep you in the loop with development we wanted to tease what we have been working on outside of the usual bug fix and quality of life improvement patches that have been going live over the last couple of months.

Patch 0.2.0, Hunter's Rise, launched in January adding a new small island to explore designed for levels 4 to 9, aiming to add additional content to do outside of the main questline and side quests in Fort Coldwraith. This was just the first half of the patch, and we are planning to have the second half ready by early April.

The second half of Hunter's Rise update will add some additional quests to complete, new rift content and a new level 10 dungeon, The Hollow Vault. This will be a 2 boss dungeon and will continue the story started in the quest 'Wayward Rookie'. We won't spill too many details as we want you to explore the dungeon and it's story for yourself, but here is a sneak peak at it's interior.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/42b5c46ec29d446673bdd2b2ebee2cb6b18883bf.png[/img]

We're excited to conclude the 0.2.0 update and begin working on the next big patch, Bandit's Hollow, which will continue the main storyline and add a additional 2 levels, bringing the max level to 12. But we'll talk more about that in the coming months.

Thanks again to everyone who has been playing the game and leaving feedback on the Steam discussion board, it's been so valuable hearing your suggestions and being able to implement them in the game, so keep it coming!

notes.title: Early Access Roadmap
notes.content:
[h1]Our plans for the future[/h1]

It's been over a week since Tundralia: The Frigid Frontier released into early access and I wanted to thank everyone for the support and positive feedback we've received so far. I would also like to give a huge thank-you to the people who have responded on the community discussion board with bugs and suggestions. We released Tundralia into early access so we can involve the community with development, so your feedback is instrumental in allowing us to know which areas of the game need more work, what bugs need squishing, and which features players would like to see in the future. We're committed to making Tundralia the best possible version of the game that it can be and we can't do that without our players.

With all that in mind, we wanted to highlight our plans for development over the course of early access. We've already released 3 small patches with ongoing polish, balancing, and bug fixes, which we'll continue doing based on the feedback we receive on the community discussion board. But what about the bigger patches around these that bring new content?

[h2]The roadmap[/h2]

Currently we have 5 major patches fully planned out that will bring the game closer to it's full 1.0.0 release. Obviously things are subject to change but no matter what, Tundralia will grow with more content as it has always been our plan for the max level to be 30, including new areas to explore with the expected content like new quests and dungeons. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/7913bea627709f3772aaa720dc02f75762c7cb74.png[/img]

This roadmap just covers the proposed content up to level 20, so once we're at patch 0.4.0 you can expect another roadmap which will conclude the proposed patches up to level 30 and patch 1.0.0. Please note that we have not put dates against each patch to ensure enough time is given for development, when things are ready for release, we'll definitely let you know!

[h2]What's next[/h2]

Finally, just to tease what's next - here's a current sneaky look behind the scenes at the in development landscape for Hunter's Rise. We'll release more details early next year, so stay tuned for that!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/90d2a5558cf90cd9f479057efb084a2005805514.png[/img]

notes.title: Feature Spotlight | Housing & Furniture
notes.content:
Welcome to the sixth (and final) feature spotlight where we delve into one of the many features of Tundralia. Ahead of tomorrows release we wanted to cover one of the newer features that we've added just in time for the launch - housing and furniture! Lets dive in.

[h1]Your house[/h1]

In Tundralia the adventure doesn’t end when you leave the battlefield. Here, owning your own home is more than just a status symbol—it’s your personal haven, a reflection of your style and creativity, and a crucial part of your gameplay experience.

Step into your very own Lonely Lodge, a cosy retreat nestled on its own island near Forth Coldwraith. Whether you’re a battle-hardened marauder seeking a place to rest, or a peaceful crafter looking to display your prized possessions, the Lonely Lodge is your blank canvas.

Just buy the deed from the furniture merchant in Fort Coldwraith, read it, and then head to the green portal at the dock to teleport to your new home!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/60c39db9bd4270684ebf608e701e1b90cb90f790.png[/img]

[h1]Furniture[/h1]

Tundralia’s housing system shines in its simplicity and flexibility. Rather than a rigid, predefined layout, you have the freedom to place furniture wherever you desire. Transform your lodge into a rustic cabin, a grand hall, or a whimsical fairy-tale home—the choice is entirely yours.

Enter decorating mode and then using the `[` and `]` keys, you can rotate each piece of furniture to achieve the perfect angle. No more settling for awkward placements; every item can be aligned to your exact specifications. Once you’ve found the perfect spot, a simple press of the `V` key secures the furniture in place. It’s as easy as that!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/8f2b3daf71922cbb1345a60d62de7306e64d8019.png[/img]

Your dream home isn’t complete without the right decor. In Tundralia, merchants scattered across the land offer a variety of furniture pieces to suit every taste and need. From simple candles and rustic tables to decorative food like a pint of beer or a loaf of bread, these merchants are your go-to source for all things home-related.

As the game develops further, expect even more customisation options, new furniture items, and enhanced interactive features. So stay tuned for more updates as we continue through early access!

Well that's it for this week's final feature spotlight, we are so excited for the release tomorrow and we can't want to hear your feedback to the game.

notes.title: Feature Spotlight | Dungeons & Rifts
notes.content:
Welcome to the fifth feature spotlight where we delve into one of the many features of Tundralia. We can't believe that the early access release is this week, so ahead of the launch lets take a look at some of the content that you'll be doing once you've reached level 10, dungeons and rifts.

[h1]Dungeons[/h1]

Dungeons are enclosed spaces found throughout the world that offer some of the greatest challenges in Tundralia, and the greatest rewards. A dungeon can be found by looking for a glowing blue portal, normally by the mouth of a cave or in front of a door. Entering a dungeon you will find several rooms and passages filled with enemies to kill. These enemies will be more deadlier than normal so are best taken one at a time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/4f49bd16ba22afd5f62ef20971c13c5d1c9e86df.png[/img]

Each dungeon will also contain 1 to 4 boss enemies to kill, these will be signified by their unique look and the '[Boss]' tag in their name. These bosses will have a larger health pool than the rest of the enemies in the dungeon as well as dangerous abilities that you will need to avoid. Successfully killing a boss will reward you with rare armour and weapons that can only be found from killing the bosses in that dungeon, so they are a great way to gear up your character to increase your stats!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/c743022f9a798b58cd696903e1124fcd45377b62.png[/img]

[h1]Rifts[/h1]

Rifts are tears between Tundralia and the unseen realm which spew out demons for you to kill. They can be found across the landscape by looking for the evil purple portal in the sky. These dynamic events spawn randomly and upon completion, the next will spawn. Just run up to the rift to receive the event quest, kill the demons as instructed and destroy the anchor crystal to summon a rift boss. These are like dungeon bosses so have more health and dangerous abilities to avoid. Upon completing a rift you will receive a corrupt soul shard that you can then use to buy rare and powerful items from the mysterious Cult of the Unseen Eye.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/ffb86eaee9733bde3e1674b55032e0286b23e000.png[/img]

Both these systems are designed to give the player challenging activities to complete outside of the questing experience. In the initial early access release there will be 1 dungeon to complete, White Fur Den located in Icetooth Ravine, and 3 variations of rifts. We plan on expanding these out in future updates though with more dungeons to complete and new variations of the rifts that can spawn.

Well that's it for this week's feature spotlight, we have one more feature spotlight to go and then it'll be time for the early access release! It's surreal that the launch is almost upon us, we can't wait for you all to play Tundralia and to hear your response to the game.

notes.title: Feature Spotlight | Reputations & Collections
notes.content:
Welcome to the fourth feature spotlight where we delve into one of the many features of Tundralia. It's an exciting time as we are now less than a month away from the early access release! Today's spotlight is all about about reputations and collections. Lets dive in!

[h1]Reputations[/h1]

As discussed in the previous feature spotlight, there are over 30 quests to complete in Tundralia. Doing these will reward you with reputation with the two factions of people that you will meet during your adventurers; The Snowborn Pioneers, and The Coldwraith Defenders. At first you will be 'Unknown' to these factions, but by completing their quests, your reputation will grow to 'Known', and then 'Respected', and finally 'Renowned'. At each reputation milestone you'll unlock new rewards to purchase from the factions associated reputation vendor. Your level of reputation with each faction can be viewed from the reputation panel accessed from your inventory. Just press the reputations button to the right of the inventory to open it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/1962fc7c357f9fa8fc48a9257d49e6549e2defa5.png[/img]

The Snowborn Pioneers are a ragtag band of adventurers who have settled in Snowborn Landing and will be the first people to introduce you to the dangers Tundralia holds. The Coldwraith Defenders are the proud peoples who live in Fort Coldwraith, you will meet these later in the story once your time at Snowborn Landing has concluded. At an 'Unknown' level of reputation, both factions will sell you chest, leg, belt, and feet armour at their reputation vendors. Then at a 'Known' level they will sell additional shoulderpads and helmets for each class, so make sure to check back at the reputation vendors frequently!

[h1]Collections[/h1]

When out exploring the world, you may find a unique item that can be picked up. These will be a part of a wider collection! Once you have collected all the items of a collection, it will reward a special prize, a minipet! To see the collections panel and your progress, it can be accessed from your inventory. Just press the collections button on the right side of the inventory to open it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/9b99ab40227abd30702b350ff4f7a39f6ca1e937.png[/img]

Collections will uncover the wider lore of Tundralia and will be hidden in hard to find locations, so make sure to keep a look out! We plan on expanding this system further to include puzzles and more unique rewards.

That's it for this week's feature spotlight, the next one will focus on the end game systems in Tundralia that you can tackle once you've reached level 10. Then it'll be time for the early access release! We can't wait for you all to play Tundralia and help shape the game into something great.

notes.title: Feature Spotlight | Quests & The World
notes.content:
Welcome to the third feature spotlight where we delve into one of the many features of Tundralia. First and foremost, we'd like to apologise for the radio silence over the last year, we have been working hard on developing Tundralia and are now ready to talk about the game features in more depth as we get ever closer to our early access release. Today's spotlight is all about the quests you'll complete in the game and the world you'll explore when doing so. Let's dive in!

[h1]Main Quests[/h1]

As you start your adventure in Tundralia you'll begin with an initial quest to speak to a watch ranger which will consequentially lead into a series of over 10 main quests that span the continent as you help to uncover a rising darkness seeking to destroy Tundralia and the people that call it home.

By completing quests you'll be rewarded with experience to increase your level, gold to purchase items, reputation that unlocks access to exclusive items sold at reputation merchants, and equipment to increase your stats.

To find a quest, just look for the yellow exclamation point (!) hovering over the head of person. By talking to them and clicking the quest title in the dialogue box, the quest shall appear on screen to accept. This quest display will include the story for why the individual needs help and what with, along with the rewards should you complete it successfully.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/401d2df24cc08fcee804eff232b4bff9939140ec.png[/img]

These main quests will direct you across the landscape and will have you meet many interesting characters. kill various dangerous creatures, or collect specific items in order to complete it's requirements. You can see all your active quests and which stage of the quests you are on via the quest tracker located under the minimap. The grey button to the left of the quest stage and be clicked to set that quest as your focus, this is required to progress with some stages of quests, like visiting a specific location. The minimap will also help direct you to the next stage of your selected quest, just look at the green arrow or circle for direction on where to go.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/c310813dad5b7e2089fb6f8d04b94345548df044.png[/img]

You can also track your quests and their progress in the quest book which can be accessed by clicking the quest book button in the bottom right corner of the screen. Just expand the current quests tab by clicking the arrow button to see all the quests you current have accepted. You can also see your completed quests and failed quests in the quest book too.

Once you've finished the quest requirements you'll usually have to return to the character you collected the quest from or be directed to someone new in order to complete it and receive your reward, then you'll be able to accept the next quest in the main story and continue your adventure.

[h1]Side & Repeatable Quests[/h1]

Outside of the main quests, and as you level up, you'll encounter over 20 side quests in the world as well. These quests will work the same as main quests and are picked up from characters in the world the same way as main quests, but will instead cover a smaller self-contained story. It might be helping a witch study the unseen magic plaguing Tundralia, or helping a tradesman look after his old pet mammoth, there's plenty of hand-crafted and unique stories to explore. Side quests will still offer plenty of rewards too and are a great way to level up your character, so make sure to complete them as well as the main quests.

Finally there are also repeatable quests which are symbolised by the blue exclamation point (!) hovering over the top of notice boards. These are smaller quests which normally task you with killing enemies and can be completed as many times as you like. These are a great way of earning reputation with the different factions that call Tundralia home, as well as earning experience to level up.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/53467f1c0066ca83bd573cf1d365320b733a77bd.png[/img]

[h1]The World[/h1]

The world of Tundralia is dangerous place, filled with interesting locales such a dense pine forests, frozen ice canyons and frigid snow fields. The quests you are tasked with will take you across these places and more!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/608817e1c1c6213a560be0f6a19629a3444c60ea.png[/img]

Over the course of early access and beyond, Tundralia will change and grow as more locations, quests and content is added so there will hopefully always be a reason to play and discover something new. Well that's it for quests and the world, thanks for reading and stay tuned for the next feature spotlight.

notes.title: Feature Spotlight l Crafting
notes.content:
Welcome to the second feature spotlight where-in each month we'll delve into one of the many features of Tundralia. Today's spotlight is all about crafting, a side feature in the game that allows you to create an array of items by gathering resources, and by learning plans and recipes.

To access crafting you'll need to visit one of the two workbenches located at either Snowborn Landing or Fort Coldwraith, interact with it with as you would any NPC and the crafting interface will appear onscreen.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/82d3e654df72c38d0212a84b8df475b68f97aec8.png[/img]
[h1][b]Crafting[/b][/h1]

The crafting interface is simple and easy to use. All of the recipes and plans you've learnt will display on the left-hand side, clicking on one will show you the reagents required to craft that item. If you have the required items within your inventory, the items will display in white, if you don't they will appear red.

Once you have all of the required reagents to craft the item, just click the 'Craft Item' button and the crafted item will appear in your inventory and the items required to craft the item, will be removed. It's that simple!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/960913251f5eb91aa7b755bdce75af1693295119.png[/img]
[h1][b]Resources[/b][/h1]

But how do you get the resources needed to craft items? In the world of Tundralia, crafting reagents can be found everywhere.

Dry Wood, which is used for crafting equipment, and Snow Cap and Icewort, two herbs used for crafting potions, can be found out in the world for you to pick-up. Thin Leather, Broken Armour and Shattered Bones drop off the various enemy creatures that call Tundralia home, and Twine Thread and Snow Wasp Bile can both be brought from merchants.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/9ac8d4624d07dfbf2b7331f66e239bdaf1d9815d.png[/img]
[h1][b]Recipes[/b][/h1]

Plans and recipes can also be brought from merchants, as well as received as a reward from certain quests. Upon starting the game you will only now how to make Bone Dust and Metal Scraps, two reagents that require Shattered Bones and Broken Armour to make. But by learning more recipes you'll be able to create potions, armour and weapons.

To learn a recipe, just right click it and press the 'Learn' button and it will be added to your recipe list in the crafting interface.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/d8303a3f0a0e4cdf3732c868b147ecf727edad68.png[/img]

And that's it for crafting, as the game continues to develop we plan for more recipes and reagents to be added for you to craft. Finally, thanks for reading and stay tuned for the next feature spotlight.

notes.title: Feature Spotlight l Combat & Classes
notes.content:
Welcome to the first feature spotlight where-in each month we'll delve into one of the many features of Tundralia. Today's feature spotlight is all about one of the core features of the game, combat and classes.

In Tundralia you play as a novice adventurer who has come to the frigid wasteland to grow their fame and fortune, one of the first things you'll do when disembarking the sky-boat to start your adventure is picking your class, either the axe-wielding marauder, spell-flinging witch, or sharp-shooting ranger.

By speaking to the different residents of Snowborn Landing you'll learn the ins and outs of each class for you to then make your decision by learning the initial 'way of the...' skill from your skill tree. This decision cannot be changed once made, so make sure you're happy with your choice otherwise you'll need to start the game again to pick a different class.

[h1][b]The Marauder[/b][/h1]

Marauders are close combat warriors, that use their rage to power their attacks. Marauders wield 1-handed axes and off-hand shields, along with more heavy plated armour. Given their close proximity to their enemies during the heat of battle, Marauders should prioritise the Strength, Fate and Ferocity stats to increase their health, crit chance and physical damage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/d30687f9452f50a5d2ed0675807635ae65651bbc.png[/img]
After learning the 'Way of the Marauder' skill, marauders will learn the 'Flame Brand' and 'Thundering Roar' skills. 'Flame Brand' is a melee attack where-in the marauder uses their fiery rage to brand their enemy, causing moderate damage. 'Thundering Roar' is another melee attack, with a slightly longer range but causing less damage as a result of it's increased range. One of these abilities can then be increased at level two to do more damage but at the cost of more mana.

Upon reaching level three, marauders can learn either 'Ragefire', an AoE ability where the marauder explodes in a ball of fiery rage to damage the enemies around them, or 'Weapon Throw', a ranged attack where the marauder hurls their weapon at their enemy. At levels four and five you can then either learn the previous abilities you haven't learnt yet or increase the power of the abilities you have learnt.

At level six you can learn 'Enrage' a 10 second buff that increases your Ferocity by 50. At level eight, 'Scorching Blow' a powerful melee attack, and at level ten, 'Burning Soul' a 60 second buff that changes your base element to fire so you receive decreased damage from holy enemies but in turn receive more damage from water enemies. Similar to levels four and five, at levels seven and nine you can either learn the previous abilities you haven't learnt yet or increase the power of the abilities you have learnt.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/e4c0c9b516eceacf3b71ce532f2f2c8d96795de4.png[/img]
[h1][b]The Witch[/b][/h1]

Witches are ranged spell casters, that use the dark magic of the unseen world to damage their enemies and heal themselves. Witches wield 2-handed staves and off-hand books, along with light wearing armour. Witches fight from afar and should prioritise the Intellect, Fate and Wisdom stats to increase their mana, crit chance and magical damage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/18f3c652d141cbae9dd98defd05d3ae4214a675c.png[/img]
After leaning the 'Way of the Witch' skill, witches will learn the 'Twist Essence' and 'Mark of Terror' skills. 'Twist Essence' is a ranged attack where-in the witch curses their enemy, causing a small amount of damage each second, over 10 seconds. 'Mark of Terror' is another ranged attack which also heals the witch for half of the damage done. One of these abilities can then be increased at level two to do more damage but at the cost of more mana.

Upon reaching level three, witches can learn either 'Fog Mind', a ranged attack that also increases the time between your enemies attacks for 10 seconds, or 'Blood Bolt' a ranged attack where the witch hurls a bolt of blood magic at their enemy causing a large amount of damage. At levels four and five you can then either learn the previous abilities you haven't learnt yet or increase the power of the abilities you have learnt.

At level six you can learn 'Surrender to Fear' a 10 second buff that regenerates your mana at the cost of your health. At level eight, 'Steal Essence' an AoE attack that also heals you for half of the damage dealt, and at level ten, 'Decaying Soul' a 60 second buff that changes your base element to death so you receive decreased damage from nature enemies but in turn receive more damage from holy enemies. Similar to levels four and five, at levels seven and nine you can either learn the previous abilities you haven't learnt yet or increase the power of the abilities you have learnt.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/b9614678bdbcdc7bd11c84d60d0a37b59e24b353.png[/img]
[h1][b]The Ranger[/b][/h1]

Rangers are hybrid combatants that use their mastery over nature to cause damage both at range and in close combat. Rangers wield 2-handed bows and off-hand quivers, along with medium leather armour. Rangers should prioritise the Fate, Ferocity and Wisdom stats to increase their crit chance, physical damage and magical damage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/3ee492e6be657c2d5c86f68eb27f697b69eb1495.png[/img]
After learning the 'Way of the Ranger' skill, rangers will learn the 'Poison Arrow' and 'Quick Shot' skills. 'Poison Arrow' is a ranged attack where-in the ranger poisons their enemy, causing a small amount of damage each second, over 10 seconds. 'Quick Shot' is another ranged attack which deals moderate damage. One of these abilities can then be increased at level two to do more damage but at the cost of more mana.

Upon reaching level three, rangers can learn either 'Ice Arrow', a ranged attack that also slows the enemies walk speed for 6 seconds, or 'Rain Arrows' an AoE attack that deals damage to the enemies in close proximity. At levels four and five you can then either learn the previous abilities you haven't learnt yet or increase the power of the abilities you have learnt.

At level six you can learn 'Call of the Wild' a 10 second buff that increases your Fate by 50 for 10 seconds. At level eight, 'Summon Crow' a damage attack where you summon a crow to claw at your enemy, and at level ten, 'Everliving Soul' a 60 second buff that changes your base element to nature so you receive decreased damage from water enemies but in turn receive more damage from death enemies. Similar to levels four and five, at levels seven and nine you can either learn the previous abilities you haven't learnt yet or increase the power of the abilities you have learnt.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/a09a6e99e451d669c3d12405ca2a6cd866a27514.png[/img]
[h1][b]Combat[/b][/h1]

Combat in Tundralia is done via a tab target hotkey system traditionally used by old school MMORPGs. Abilities are learnt from the skill tree and dragged to the hotbar at the bottom of the screen. To activate a ability, you can either press it's associated hotkey or double click the icon on the hotbar, costing mana and putting the ability into a state of cooldown where in it cannot be activated again until the cooldown is over. Enemies are then selected either using the tab button or by clicking on them.

Combat will then consist of activating abilities in succession, and when they are not on cooldown, to damage your enemies. Once your enemies health reaches zero, they will die and drop items for you to pick-up. This will need to be done while ensuring you have enough mana to cast spells and that your own health doesn't go below zero, as if it does, you will die and respawn at the nearest graveyard.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41645171/10ed04da825bcd517b74e0571f8709971ef471d2.png[/img]
And that's it for classes and combat, as the game continues to develop there may be changes made to the abilities mentioned for each class, and new ones added as we aim for combat in Tundralia to be ever evolving as game itself develops. Finally, thanks for reading and stay tuned for the next feature spotlight.
